subject: What Changed to Your Credit Card Today? Edition 14
summary: HDFC raises the fuel surcharge waiver ceiling on the Titanium Times Card and adds a new perks block, cashback, fuel waiver, and a renewal fee waiver, to the Platinum Times Card.
body_html:
Today's a quieter one, both changes belong to HDFC Bank, and both sit on cards from HDFC's older "Times" series, the Titanium Times and Platinum Times credit cards. These are cards most people picked up years ago through the Times of India loyalty tie-up, not ones HDFC is actively selling today. If you don't hold either, feel free to skim past. If you do, there are a few rupees worth caring about here.

Titanium Times Card

HDFC's own page for this card now sets the fuel surcharge waiver ceiling at ₹5,000 per transaction, up from ₹4,000. The waiver itself hasn't moved: it's still 1% of the surcharge, capped at ₹250 a month. What changed is which fill-ups even qualify.

Say you top up ₹4,500 worth of petrol in one go, and the card charges the usual 1% fuel surcharge on that, about ₹45. Under the old ₹4,000 ceiling, that surcharge fell outside the waiver band entirely, you paid the ₹45 yourself. With the ceiling now at ₹5,000, that same ₹4,500 fill-up qualifies, and HDFC picks up the surcharge instead.

The catch: I'm flagging this cautiously. This is HDFC's own product page showing the new number today, the bank appears to have updated their marketing page copy, and we haven't found independent confirmation of it yet. Treat it as what HDFC's site currently says, not a fully corroborated fact, until you've actually tested it at the pump.

Platinum Times Credit Card

This one's a bigger addition. Until today, the Platinum Times Card's tracked page didn't carry an "Other Perks" section at all. Today it showed up with four items in it: up to 5% cashback on utility bills and shopping, a 1% fuel surcharge waiver on transactions between ₹400 and ₹5,000 capped at ₹500 a month, a renewal fee waiver if you spend ₹2.5 lakh on the card in a year, and the option to convert big purchases into EMI after the fact.

Worth noticing on its own: the fuel waiver cap here is ₹500 a month, double the ₹250 cap on the Titanium Times Card above, on the same 1% rate and the same ₹400 to ₹5,000 band. If you fill up consistently and hit that cap every month, that's up to ₹6,000 a year in surcharge you'd no longer be paying out of pocket, assuming you were paying it before.

The catch: same caution as above, and doubly so here, since this is a full new section appearing rather than a single number moving. This reads like HDFC copying its standard "Other Perks" block over from a sibling card, but we haven't found independent confirmation that these benefits are actually live on your account. If you hold this card, I'd call HDFC or check your next statement before assuming the ₹2.5 lakh renewal waiver or the cashback line is active, rather than taking the page at face value.

What I'd actually do with this

If you hold the Titanium Times Card and regularly fill fuel above ₹4,000 in one go, this quietly puts a little more money back in your pocket. It's a real change if it holds, just not one worth restructuring your fill-up habits around for a ₹45-odd saving.

If you hold the Platinum Times Card, this is worth an actual phone call to HDFC before you count on any of it. A renewal fee waiver and a cashback line appearing out of nowhere is good news if it's real and live on your account, but the honest answer right now is that we've only seen it on the bank's page, not confirmed it in practice.

For everyone else, neither of these cards is one I'd go apply for off the back of today's changes. Both are older cards HDFC has stopped actively selling to new applicants, and the numbers involved, even if every word of today's changes turns out true, are modest.

This is my honest read, not formal financial advice. I'm not your advisor, and before you act on anything here, run it past a professional or at least sleep on it. But this is exactly how I'd think about it if these were my cards.

Monzy
